note: Generated by tools/editor_filters.mjs from src-filters. Transmission is on-axis, 0-1; sensors normalised to their own peak.

sensorNotes.Sony A7III full spectrum (measured to 80: Measured 300-800nm on a real converted body by JMC Scientific Consulting Ltd (Dr Jonathan Crowther), published in J. Imaging 2022, 8, 54 (doi:10.3390/jimaging8030054, CC BY 4.0); traced from the paper’s Figure 1f. Past 800nm it is modelled: the colour filters stop separating the channels (same paper) and the response falls with silicon’s.
sensorNotes.Canon 5DS R full spectrum (measured to 8: Measured 300-800nm on a real converted body (internal UV/IR filter removed, colour filter array kept) by Dr Jonathan Crowther (JMC Scientific Consulting Ltd), published in The Imaging Science Journal 2019, 67, 268-276 (doi:10.1080/13682199.2019.1638664); traced from the paper’s Figure 5b. Past 800nm it is modelled the same way as the Sony A7III. The one to use for a converted Canon.
sensorNotes.Generic CMOS (approximation): A generic approximation, not a measured camera; no data past 1000nm.
sensorNotes.Kodak KAF-8300 CCD (real, astronomy): A real measured sensor, but an astronomy CCD, not a camera body.
sensorNotes.Canon 40D full spectrum (MaxMax, measure: Measured on a real converted body by MaxMax (LDP LLC) with a monochromator, 375-1000nm, and traced from their published chart; past 1000nm it follows the fall-off SurfLabX measured on a modern full-spectrum sensor. Use with care: above about 840nm its three channels do not come together, which the direct measurements of other converted cameras show they should (Crowther 2022, Sony A7 III; Aphalo 2024, Olympus E-M1), so the values were probably read after white balance or a colour conversion in Photoshop. The default Sony A7 III curve is the safer choice. For a converted Canon, the Canon 5DS R curve (measured directly) is the safer choice.
